newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian railways say Pacific grain moves improve.
newsitem.headline: Canadian railways say Pacific grain moves improve.

text.p: Canadian railway companies said Monday they unloaded more hopper cars carrying grains and oilseeds at Pacific ports in the past week than recently.
"It's been better than the last couple of weeks and it's headed in the right direction," Canadian National Railway Co spokesman Jim Feeny told Reuters.
Canada's grain handling system is so congested 41 ships waited to load at Pacific ports Friday for up to 43 days.
The backlog lead to an emergency meeting of the grain and rail industries in Calgary late Thursday where the Canadian Wheat Board said it may ship grain via the United States.
CWB said it faces C$15 million in demurrage fines because of the delays since early January and passed on February and March sales while April sales were in jeopardy.
CN unloaded 1,156 hopper cars in Prince Rupert in the week ended 0600 PST compared to the targetted 1,300 car, or 88.9 percent of allocations, Feeny said.
It unloaded 74 percent of its assigned cars in Prince Rupert in the prior week.
CN unloaded 941 hopper cars in Vancouver in the week ended 0600 PST Monday compared to the targetted 1,100 cars, or 85.5 percent of allocations, he said.
It unloaded 97 percent of its assigned cars in Vancouver in the prior week.
Combined, CN's unloads at Pacific ports reached 87 percent of the past week's allocations.
"We lost the mainline at Clearwater subdivision for a day and a half last week to a derailment," Feeny added.
Canadian Pacific Ltd unit CP Rail System reported sporadic weekend grain shipments.
"It's been mixed. It's been miserable in Winnipeg and Saskatchewan with the blowing snow over the weekend and cold temperatures," CP spokesman Steve Morris said.

Air brakes on locomotives function less effectively below -25 degrees Celsius because the temperature thins the air so that a 100-unit train hauled by three locomotives at -25 C requires six engines at -40 Celsius (-40 F), Morris said.
"But in Alberta the weather wasn't too bad so things are coming along quite well actually," Morris added.
